units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
Turns back towards the dining-room.
Aren't you coming too, Oswald?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: From within.
No, thank you. I think I shall go out a little.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Yes, do. The weather seems a little brighter now.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: She shuts the dining-room door, goes to the hall door, and calls:.
Regina!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Outside.
Yes, Mrs. Alving?
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Go down to the laundry, and help with the garlands.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Yes, Mrs. Alving.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: MRS. ALVING assures herself that REGINA goes; then shuts the door.
I suppose he cannot overhear us in there?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Not when the door is shut. Besides, he's just going out.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: I am still quite upset. I don't know how I could swallow a morsel of dinner.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Controlling her nervousness, walks up and down.
Nor I. But what is to be done now?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Yes; what is to be done? I am really quite at a loss. I am so utterly without experience in matters of this sort.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: I feel sure that, so far, no mischief has been done.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: No; heaven forbid! But it is an unseemly state of things, nevertheless.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: It is only an idle fancy on Oswald's part; you may be sure of that.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Well, as I say, I am not accustomed to affairs of the kind. But I should certainly think--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Out of the house she must go, and that immediately. That is as clear as daylight--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Yes, of course she must.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: But where to? It would not be right to--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Where to? Home to her father, of course.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: To whom did you say?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: To her--But then, Engstrand is not--? Good God, Mrs. Alving, it's impossible! You must be mistaken after all.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Unfortunately there is no possibility of mistake. Johanna confessed everything to me; and Alving could not deny it. So there was nothing to be done but to get the matter hushed up.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: No, you could do nothing else.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: The girl left our service at once, and got a good sum of money to hold her tongue for the time. The rest she managed for herself when she got to town. She renewed her old acquaintance with Engstrand, no doubt let him see that she had money in her purse, and told him some tale about a foreigner who put in here with a yacht that summer. So she and Engstrand got married in hot haste. Why, you married them yourself.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: But then how to account for--? I recollect distinctly Engstrand coming to give notice of the marriage. He was quite overwhelmed with contrition, and bitterly reproached himself for the misbehaviour he and his sweetheart had been guilty of.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes; of course he had to take the blame upon himself.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: But such a piece of duplicity on his part! And towards me too! I never could have believed it of Jacob Engstrand. I shall not fail to take him seriously to task; he may be sure of that.--And then the immorality of such a connection! For money--! How much did the girl receive?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Three hundred dollars.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Just think of it--for a miserable three hundred dollars, to go and marry a fallen woman!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Then what have you to say of me? I went and married a fallen man.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Why--good heavens!--what are you talking about! A fallen man!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Do you think Alving was any purer when I went with him to the altar than Johanna was when Engstrand married her?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Well, but there is a world of difference between the two cases--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Not so much difference after all--except in the price:--a miserable three hundred dollars and a whole fortune.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: How can you compare such absolutely dissimilar cases? You had taken counsel with your own heart and with your natural advisers.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Without looking at him.
I thought you understood where what you call my heart had strayed to at the time.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Distantly.
